questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personally knowing the language, and being personally interested in the culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Sorbonne university were particularly good at giving information on where to find all administrative facilities like getting student ID, place of exchange and social activities for students. You had a personal contact whom you could ask questions in case there were issues.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received no assistance upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire is a large student campus for international exchange students in Paris. It's a wonderful place with lots of green areas, opportunities for socializing and meeting like-minded students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchen facilities were available. A cafeteria was available, but few people used it, but the quality is decent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a good idea is to apply in advance, since there's a limited number of spots. But the pricing, location and quality are excellent, and students who previously lived outside campus and joined later vastly preferred student life in the Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All registrations for courses were planned directly with our contact at the university. The process was quite smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help is through direct dialogue with your contact at the university, and my contact was very helpful in explaining which courses were available and how many I needed to fulfill my ECTS point goals.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Since I applied quite late, few courses were left. But I got the courses and internships I wanted since the selection is quite large.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
As long as you're studying Medicine at KU, prioritize on picking courses you're interested in rather than taking courses and internships you're interested in since the language barrier makes 
Also, take with your contact person if you're in doubt, they're very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 20 ECTS point exchange with 12 weeks of internship with morning classes at the hospital.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more paternalistic and less freeform than in Copenhagen. Classes are longer and studying is situated in the classroom, compared to in Denmark where there are relatively few classes but more time for studying at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 12 weeks of internship at Pitié Salpêtrière with classes in the morning at the hospital.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Diabetology at Pitié Salpêtrière was excellent.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Unexpected costs were mostly personal spending since the cultural and travel opportunities are so great.
Plan how much you want to spend in advance, and try to put some extra aside, as you'll find things like theatres, concerts, and travel opportunities while down here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Travelling internally in France is very cheap, with high-speed trains (the TGV) going for below 30-40€

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Cité Universitaire Sports club is very affordable (20€ per month) and provides access to >30 activities including tennis, swimming, volleyball etc. You'll definitely find something you like.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel to other major French cities like Lyon, Bordeaux and Marseille. Hike in the French alps, visit Vinyards, sail on a boat, wander in forests. France is more than just Paris.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Book train tickets 4-6 weeks in advance and go on weekend trips to other major French cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Since I was quite well prepared, the language and culture were quite easy to adjust to. Speaking to patients, writing notes and letters was doable, and after 1 month became second nature. 
But in case you haven't studied French since High-school, expect to spend a lot of time studying the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sorbonne Université has a lot of great social activities, as well as the Cité Universitaire. Sign up and go meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way of studying and practicing medicine is very different compared to the Danish model. Clinical internships end at 6 pm, so you're usually quite tired at the end of the day. The tasks you're given are also different, where in Denmark you're more involved in panning treatments for patients and ordering blood samples, tests and ordering medications practically by yourself, in France you're more a support to the doctors, where you write their notes, write letters and contact other departments and physicians regarding second opinions.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really admire the French systematic approach to diagnosing patients and treatment. There's a lot more continuity where it's the same doctors at each department for several weeks in a row, instead of in Denmark where each physician is at a department for a few days before rotating to the next post.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn French in advance so you can focus on your studies and enjoying the culture and city once you're in Paris.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I personally thought I'd have time to work on a research project from back home in Denmark during my exchange, but postponed this, to focus on studies and cultural activities. 
If possible, don't bring to many work-tasks from Denmark with you, and just enjoy your stay in Paris.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other french students and working alongside the french doctors.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to practice medicine in a new environment. Not because the language was different, but because the way you write notes, order diagnostic tests and administer treatment are quite different from the way it is done in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
